english.title: Person under the control of Registrar General for Scotland disclose personal census information without authorisation
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), Registrar General for Scotland, disclose, personal census informationwithout lawful authority, to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 8(2)(a) and (5) of the Census Act 1920.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
person under control of the Registrar General for Scotland disclosed
disclosed without authority to another person
personal census information

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 8(4) of the Census Act 1920 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove that at the time of the alleged offence he / she believed that they were acting with lawful authority; or that the information in question was not personal census information; and that they had no reasonable cause to believe otherwise.
(ii) Section 8(6) of the Census Act 1920 provides that for the purposes of this offence a person is to be treated as under the control of the Registrar General for Scotland if he / she is, or has been employed by that Registrar (whether or not on a full-time basis); or otherwise employed, or acting, (whether or not on a full-time basis) as part of that Registrar's staff for purposes of the Act.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
